claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is primarily governed by formation of a stable, adherent passive oxide film.
Nanoscale compositional homogeneity induced by high configurational entropy causes the stable passive oxide film to form.
A uniform passive film acts synergistically with high substrate hardness to mitigate combined mechanical and corrosive degradation.
Thermomechanical and surface treatments can enhance nanoscale compositional homogeneity.
Increasing nanoscale compositional homogeneity promotes formation of a uniform passive oxide film.
High configurational entropy forces a homogeneous distribution of multiple elements in high-entropy alloys.
Homogeneous elemental distribution facilitates formation of a consistent and adherent oxide layer.
The passive oxide film impedes corrosive attack.
Strong adhesion of the passive film reinforces the substrate against mechanical wear.
The passive film and substrate together form a barrier that limits overall material degradation.
An engineered high-entropy alloy will exhibit significantly lower total material loss during combined wear-corrosion testing than a conventional alloy matched for bulk mechanical properties.
The engineered high-entropy alloy will exhibit less wear than the matched conventional alloy.
The engineered high-entropy alloy will exhibit less pitting corrosion than the matched conventional alloy.
The combined degradation rate will be substantially lower than the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only degradation rates.
The predicted benefit should hold at moderate temperature and pH when the passive film remains intact.
The predicted benefit may fail at very high temperatures or in highly acidic or basic environments because the passive film may break down.
Local compositional variations and processing inconsistencies can influence passive-film integrity and wear performance.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in material loss, pit formation, and passive-film stability relative to the matched conventional alloy would falsify the proposed mechanism.
